Let me start by understanding the situation better. My sister is 19, and she's a lot younger than me. I think she was spoiled growing up because our parents didn't have as much money when I was a kid, so she got to go on vacations and do other things that I wasn't able to do. Now, she's controlling and gets mad at me over really small things, like peeing a bit on the toilet seat, forgetting to fill the Brita water filter, or leaving a single pot out at night to be washed in the morning. She calls these things 'disrespectful,' but I don't get why they bother her so much and why she can't let things go. Yesterday, she was making dinner for herself, my mom, and my dad, and I was doing something else. I went to put something in the oven, and she said, "I needed that for anything." I told her to just chill, that we can split the oven or she can wait 20 minutes. She got mad, and I got fed up with her attitude and told her that the world doesn't revolve around her. She scoffed and said the same back to me. I told her that her attitude was going to get her into trouble in the real world, and she said, "Think I'll be just fine, but thanks for the advice." I'm wondering if I did the right thing by telling her that. Is it wrong to tell someone that the world doesn't revolve around them? Or is it okay because she's being controlling and unreasonable? I don't know why she hates me so much and is so controlling. Maybe it's because she was spoiled growing up, and now she's struggling to deal with things not always going her way. On one hand, I think it's important to stand up for yourself and not let someone control you. If she's being unreasonable, it's okay to set boundaries. But on the other hand, telling someone that the world doesn't revolve around them might come off as dismissive or unkind. Maybe there's a better way to communicate that without making her feel attacked. I also wonder if there's a deeper issue here. Maybe her controlling behavior is a way of dealing with her own insecurities or frustrations. If that's the case, maybe I should approach the situation with more empathy rather than confrontation. But at the same time, I don't want to enable her behavior by letting her control me. Perhaps I should consider talking to her about her feelings and why she reacts the way she does. Understanding her perspective might help me address the issue more effectively. However, I'm not sure if she's open to that kind of conversation, especially since she seems to get defensive easily. In the end, I think it's a balance between standing up for myself and showing empathy. Maybe there's a way to assert my boundaries without making her feel like the world doesn't revolve around her. It's a tricky situation, and I'm not entirely sure what the right approach is.
